﻿Looks good, @JHON12091986. That version is correct now, 32768 keeps you safely under every engine's argument limit and `subarray` avoids the per-chunk copy.

Two small optional notes, take them or leave them:
- The `if (uint8.length <= 32768)` fast path is redundant. For any length up to the chunk size the loop already runs exactly once over the whole array, so you can drop the special case without changing behavior.
- `Math.min(i + CHUNK_SIZE, uint8.length)` is also unnecessary, since `subarray` clamps the end index for you. `uint8.subarray(i, i + CHUNK_SIZE)` is enough.

Whichever version lands, it would be good to cover it with tests: empty view, byte preservation across all 256 values, `byteOffset`/`byteLength` handling, and a large buffer (e.g. 200k) that used to throw. #36941 already includes those if it is useful as a reference.

Since #36936 and #36941 are the same fix, maybe we coordinate so only one PR proceeds and avoid making the maintainers review duplicates.
